chunks: To God belongs all that is in the heavens and the earth; and whether you reveal what is in your heart or conceal it, you will have to account for it to God who will pardon whom He please and punish whom He will, for God has the power over all things.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about God's knowledge of our inner thoughts and intentions?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse (Ayat al-Hisab) is pivotal in the theological debate regarding the scope of divine accountability, with scholars like Al-Tabarsi and Al-Kulayni discussing whether 'what is in your souls' refers specifically to intentions or encompasses all inner states. It underscores the balance between God's absolute power (Qadir) and His mercy (Ghaffar), illustrating that while God holds humans to account for their hidden thoughts, He exercises discretion in forgiveness, a concept central to the Shia understanding of divine justice and the intercession of the Ahl al-Bayt.
